# C4 system context

**Use when:** you need the big picture for any audience: your system as one box, the people who use it and the systems it depends on.

## Purpose
Level 1 of Simon Brown's C4 model. It answers "what is this system, who uses it and
what does it talk to?" with no technology detail. It is the diagram for executives,
new joiners and the first page of any architecture document.

## Spec settings
- `"type": "c4-context"`, `"layout": "flowchart-lr"` (people left, system in the
  middle, external systems right). `flowchart-tb` also works (people on top).
- Theme `auto` -> `c4` (blue system, grey externals, person shapes).

## Node kinds
| Kind | Use for |
|---|---|
| `person` | A role or persona: `Customer`, `Back-Office Clerk`. |
| `system` | The system in scope - exactly ONE node, usually with `emphasis: true`. |
| `external-system` | Every other software system: `Payment Provider`, `ERP`, `Email Service`. |

Each node gets a one-sentence `description` of its responsibility: C4 boxes are
self-describing. No `technology` at this level (or at most a vendor name for an
external system).

Never put containers here - no databases, queues, APIs, functions or cloud services
(`[c4-context]`). If you want to show them, that is a `c4-container` diagram.

## Groups
Usually none. An `enterprise` boundary (kind `boundary`) can frame the systems your
organization owns; external systems stay outside it (`[external-placement]`).

## Edges
- Every edge labeled with what the relationship is for, as a verb phrase:
  `places orders using`, `sends emails via`, `gets stock levels from`.
- Leave protocols out at this level; they belong in the container view.
- Arrow points in the direction of the dependency/initiation.

## Checklist
- [ ] Exactly one system in scope, emphasized
- [ ] All people and external systems that interact with it - and nothing inside it
- [ ] Every element has a short description
- [ ] Every edge has a verb-phrase label
- [ ] Title `<System> - System Context`; subtitle with scope and date

## Common mistakes
- Showing internal parts (databases, microservices).
- Unlabeled relationships.
- Systems named by technology (`Kafka`) instead of purpose (`Event Platform`).
- Including people who never touch the system.

## Example
```json
{
  "title": "Internet Banking - System Context",
  "subtitle": "C4 level 1 - Oct 2026",
  "type": "c4-context",
  "layout": "flowchart-lr",
  "nodes": [
    {"id": "customer", "label": "Personal Customer", "kind": "person", "description": "Holds one or more bank accounts."},
    {"id": "banking", "label": "Internet Banking", "kind": "system", "emphasis": true, "description": "Lets customers view balances and make payments."},
    {"id": "mainframe", "label": "Core Banking", "kind": "external-system", "description": "Stores accounts and transactions."},
    {"id": "email", "label": "Email System", "kind": "external-system", "description": "Microsoft Exchange server."}
  ],
  "edges": [
    {"source": "customer", "target": "banking", "label": "views accounts using"},
    {"source": "banking", "target": "mainframe", "label": "gets account data from"},
    {"source": "banking", "target": "email", "label": "sends emails via"},
    {"source": "email", "target": "customer", "label": "sends emails to"}
  ]
}
```
